selectionCriteria.complexityMinimum: Must include frontend, backend, database, auth, RBAC, workflow, audit, tests, docs
selectionCriteria.complexityMaximum: Must be completable by a single run in under 200 message turns per run
selectionCriteria.nonFactoryRequirement: No Factory governance, verifier, self-reference, agent framework, or benchmark shortcuts
selectionCriteria.comparabilityRequirement: Same project spec, same acceptance criteria, three comparable runs A/B/C
selectionCriteria.evaluabilityRequirement: Must have objective measurable quality dimensions beyond file/export/agent counts

rejectedAlternatives.name: E-commerce platform
rejectedAlternatives.reason: Too large - payment, inventory, shopping cart expand scope beyond comparable runs

rejectedAlternatives.name: Blog/Content CMS
rejectedAlternatives.reason: Too small - insufficient role complexity, no workflow lifecycle to expose simplification

rejectedAlternatives.name: Chat application
rejectedAlternatives.reason: Too narrow - lacks audit, workflow, permissions depth needed for role-agent comparison

rejectedAlternatives.name: API-only microservice
rejectedAlternatives.reason: No frontend - cannot evaluate full-stack delivery quality across runs

rejectedAlternatives.name: Factory-style governance tool
rejectedAlternatives.reason: Self-referential - violates non-Factory requirement, Factory would have unfair advantage

justification.complexityJustification: TeamFlow Lite has 11 distinct cross-cutting concerns. Complex enough to surface differences between Vanilla, Factory Lite, and Factory Role-Agent approaches.
justification.sizeJustification: Estimated scope: ~15-25 API endpoints, ~8-12 database tables, ~6-10 UI pages. Small enough for single run, large enough to demand organization.
justification.simplificationRiskExposure: Multi-tenant isolation, role-based permission boundaries, audit trail completeness, and workflow state transitions are areas where sloppy shortcuts are tempting but detectable.
relevantRoles: Architect (data model, API design, component tree)
Frontend Developer (UI components, state management, forms)
QA Engineer (test suite, edge cases, error states)
Tech Writer (README, API docs, run instructions)
objectiveEvaluationDimensions: API contract correctness (endpoint completeness, error codes, validation)
UI state coverage (loading, empty, error, success, edge cases)
Audit trail completeness (all important actions logged)
Test coverage and quality (not just count, but meaningful assertions)

included: User registration and login with JWT or session auth
Role-based access: owner, admin, member, viewer
Task CRUD with title, description, priority, status
Task status workflow: todo, in_progress, blocked, done
Search/filter/sort tasks by status, assignee, priority, due date
Input validation on all forms and API endpoints
Error handling with meaningful error messages
Tests: unit + integration covering auth, CRUD, workflow, permissions

technologyStack.recommendedFrontend: React or any SPA framework of runner choice
technologyStack.constraint: Must be runnable with a single command
